title: Clear the gate: how learning quests work
summary: Show how you break a small coding problem into a testable first step.
brief: A beginner Python program should greet a player by name. What is the best first quest step?
choices: Write the smallest function, try one example name, and check the exact output
Install every Python package first
Copy a large application before deciding what the greeting should do
explanation: A small, testable first slice gives you a clear success condition. Clearing this trial unlocks the learning rooms.

title: Think in steps
summary: Practise breaking a new problem into smaller questions before reaching for a solution.
brief: A client reports that a page is slow. You have not seen the code yet. What is the best first move?
choices: Rewrite the whole page immediately
Ask when it feels slow, reproduce it, and inspect measurements
Add a bigger server without checking anything
explanation: Good engineers make a problem observable first. Reproduce it, gather evidence, then choose a focused fix.

title: Debug with evidence
summary: Use a failing example, one hypothesis at a time, and a small verified change.
brief: A function returns 12 when you expect 10. Which next step gives you the clearest signal?
choices: Change several lines at once and try again
Write down the input, expected output, actual output, then inspect the relevant step
Delete the test because it is blocking you
explanation: A small reproducible case and one hypothesis at a time help isolate the cause and prove the fix.

title: How a web request works
summary: Connect browser UI, an HTTP request, server logic, and a database response.
brief: A user presses Save in a web form. Which sequence is the most typical?
choices: Browser sends a request → server validates and saves → server responds → UI shows the result
Database updates itself → browser guesses the result
Browser sends HTML directly to another user's screen
explanation: The client sends a request; the server validates and performs authorized changes, then returns a response the interface can render.

title: Make a safe team change
summary: Practise small commits, readable diffs, and clear handoffs with collaborators.
brief: You are changing a shared codebase. Which habit makes review and rollback easiest?
choices: Bundle unrelated changes into one enormous commit
Make a focused change, inspect the diff, and describe why it is needed
Edit directly on the production server
explanation: Focused changes with an understandable diff are easier to review, discuss, and safely revert.

title: Use AI, verify the work
summary: Treat an AI coding assistant as a collaborator whose output still needs evidence and review.
brief: An AI assistant proposes a database migration. What should you do before shipping it?
choices: Apply it directly because the assistant is confident
Review the schema impact, test it on representative data, and inspect the resulting diff
Ask the assistant to remove the checks
explanation: AI can speed up exploration, but the engineer remains responsible for correctness, security, and the final change.

title: Ship a useful slice
summary: Turn a broad idea into a small, testable feature with a clear user outcome.
brief: Your team has one day to improve a learning app. What is the strongest first delivery?
choices: A complete redesign with no time to validate
One learner-requested feature with a clear acceptance check and a working end-to-end path
A slide deck describing features for a later team
explanation: A narrow feature that works from user action through saved result creates useful evidence and invites feedback.

title: Show your work clearly
summary: Practise describing the problem, your contribution, and the evidence that a project works.
brief: You are presenting a project to a potential teammate. What makes your explanation most useful?
choices: List every technology name without context
Explain the user problem, your specific decisions, trade-offs, and how you verified the result
Say that AI wrote everything so you do not need to understand it
explanation: Strong project evidence connects a real problem to your contribution and shows how you checked the outcome.

title: Build a semantic page
summary: Use structure, labels, and layout to make a clear, accessible interface.
brief: A form has three unlabeled inputs. What is the strongest first fix?
choices: Add visible, programmatically associated labels
Make every input wider
Hide field names in placeholder text
explanation: Labels help everyone understand a field and work with assistive technology.

title: Model state clearly
summary: Use predictable values and types to describe a small feature.
brief: A quantity can be missing or a positive integer. Which TypeScript type fits?
choices: string
number | undefined
any
explanation: A narrow union expresses the real states and lets the compiler help.

title: Build a reusable React component
summary: Separate data from rendering and keep UI updates predictable.
brief: A saved-jobs list changes after a user clicks Save. What should drive the update?
choices: A React state update
Directly editing a DOM node
Reloading the browser
explanation: State updates let React render the new data consistently.

title: Write a small Python function
summary: Practise parameters, return values, collections, and clear names.
brief: A function averages a list and must handle empty input. What is a useful first step?
choices: Define the empty-input behavior and test both cases
Divide by list length without checking it
Print a number instead of returning it
explanation: Make the edge case explicit and verify ordinary and empty inputs.

title: Design a Python API endpoint
summary: Connect Python business logic to a request and a validated response.
brief: A FastAPI endpoint receives a new profile. Where should constraints be checked?
choices: At the API boundary with a validated request model
Only in the browser
After the database has saved it
explanation: Validation at the boundary prevents malformed data from moving deeper.

title: Persist data safely
summary: Use database transactions and parameterized queries for persistent changes.
brief: A submitted value will be used in SQL. What is the safe approach?
choices: Use parameterized queries or an ORM and validate input
Concatenate raw text into SQL
Trust the browser to block malicious input
explanation: Parameterization prevents user text from becoming executable SQL.

title: Build a Node API route
summary: Handle HTTP methods, status codes, request validation, and useful errors.
brief: A client creates a resource successfully. Which response is clearest?
choices: Return 201 with the created resource or its location
Return 500 with no body
Return 200 before the save
explanation: 201 communicates successful resource creation.

title: Connect relational records
summary: Model tables, keys, constraints, and joins for application data.
brief: A booking belongs to one account. How should the relationship be represented?
choices: A booking row with a foreign key to its account
Copy account details into every booking
Store both IDs in free-text notes
explanation: A foreign key keeps the relationship explicit and enforces integrity.

title: Agree on an API contract
summary: Make frontend and backend agree on routes, payloads, and error states.
brief: Teams are building in parallel. What helps them integrate early?
choices: Document an example request, response, and error contract
Wait until both sides are finished
Use different field names on each side
explanation: A shared contract makes parallel work testable early.

title: Test behavior at the right level
summary: Choose unit, integration, and end-to-end checks that catch real failures.
brief: A bug appears when a form calls the API and refreshes its list. Which test is direct evidence?
choices: An integration test for that form-to-API flow
A snapshot of an unrelated heading
No test; click it manually
explanation: Test the boundary where the observed failure happens.

title: Protect a user-owned record
summary: Check authentication, authorization, validation, and safe error handling.
brief: A user changes an invoice ID in a request. What must the server check?
choices: Whether the authenticated user may access that invoice
Only that the ID is a number
Whether the UI hid the button
explanation: Authorization belongs on the server for every protected object.

title: Make a reviewable Git change
summary: Use branches, commits, and pull requests to collaborate safely.
brief: A feature includes unrelated formatting across many files. What next?
choices: Split or revert unrelated changes and submit a focused diff
Commit everything without checking it
Rewrite shared main history
explanation: Focused changes are easier to review, discuss, and roll back.

title: Ship and observe a service
summary: Deploy with configuration, health checks, logs, and a rollback path.
brief: A deployment succeeds but users get errors. What should you inspect?
choices: Health checks, logs, and recent changes; roll back if needed
Assume deploy success means healthy behavior
Delete logs to clear errors
explanation: Observe the running service; deployment completion is not enough.

title: Trace a Spring request
summary: Apply the same full-stack ideas with Java and Spring.
brief: Where is a typical Spring REST endpoint exposed?
choices: A controller method mapped to an HTTP route
A CSS selector
A database backup file
explanation: Controllers map HTTP requests into logic and responses.

title: Trace an ASP.NET request
summary: Transfer API, data, and testing concepts to C# and .NET.
brief: An ASP.NET endpoint receives an invalid create request. Where is the check useful?
choices: At the request boundary, with domain rules in the service
Only after writing the record
In a comment beside the form
explanation: Validate external input at the boundary and preserve domain rules.

title: Handle an error in Go
summary: Build explicit error handling into a small Go service.
brief: A Go function returns a value and an error. What should the caller do?
choices: Check the error and choose an intentional response
Ignore it if the value is non-zero
Panic for every expected validation error
explanation: Go makes errors explicit so callers can recover or report them.

title: Validate a Laravel request
summary: Use framework validation and routes to build a safe PHP feature.
brief: Where should Laravel validate an incoming profile update?
choices: With request validation before persistence
Only in the browser
After sending the success response
explanation: Request validation creates a clear boundary before data changes.

title: Ship an end-to-end feature
summary: Plan, implement, test, and explain a feature from screen to storage.
brief: Which portfolio slice best proves full-stack ability?
choices: A working accessible UI, validated API, saved data, tests, and a trade-off note
A screenshot of a blank dashboard
A list of languages without a project
explanation: A complete vertical slice demonstrates decisions across the stack.
